newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief appoints team with few new faces.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief appoints team with few new faces.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Tuesday announced 19 senior appointments, most of whom had served under his predecessor, Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt.
Boutros-Ghali's reappointment was blocked by the United States, which accused him of being insufficiently committed to reform of the U.N. bureaucracy and reducing its spending.

"Change needs to be managed," said Fred Eckhard, an American who was confirmed as chief U.N. spokesman succeeding Sylvana Foa, also an American. "Rome wasn't built in a day," he said. "He (Annan) will implement these changes incrementally throughout this year and next year."
Among the new faces appointed by Annan, who took over as secretary-general on Jan. 1, are the heads of two key departments -- peacekeeping and political affairs. Both received three-year contracts.

For undersecretary-general in charge of peacekeeping operations, Annan's job before becoming secretary-general, he chose Bernard Miyet, France's representative to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.

The appointment was widely thought to be a reward for France, which had backed Boutros-Ghali for re-election last month but then dropped its veto against Annan after the Ghanaian was supported by all other Security Council members.

A British diplomat, Sir Kieran Prendergast, was named as undersecretary-general for political affairs, to succeed Marrack Goulding, also a Briton. Prendergast has served most recently as Britain's ambassador to Turkey and before that as high commissioner to Kenya. He was a member of Britain's U.N. mission in New York from 1979 to 1982.
No woman was appointed as an undersecretary-general but Eckhard said Annan was considering choosing a woman as a deputy secretary-general.

Of the two women among the new appointments, Angela King of Jamaica was promoted to assistant secretary-general and will serve as a general adviser on the advancement of women, reporting to Annan. Gillian Martin Sorensen will be an assistant secretary-general for external or public affairs, presumably to explain the United Nations to American groups and members of Congress. She is the wife of Theodore Sorensen, who was special counsel to President John Kennedy.

Annan previously had announced his chief advisers serving in his cabinet and replaced most of Boutros-Ghali's aides and cut down their numbers. The cabinet is headed by Iqbal Riza of Pakistan, formerly Annan's deputy in peacekeeping.
Other undersecretaries-general appointments included:
-- Nitin Desai of India, for sustainable development.
-- Yongjian Jin of China, for development support and management services.
-- Yasushi Akashi of Japan, for humanitarian affairs.
-- Joseph Connor of the United States, for administration and management.
-- Hans Corell of Sweden, for legal affairs.
Other assistant secretaries-general appointments included:
-- Jean-Claude Aime of Haiti, Boutros-Ghali's cabinet chief, transferred as head of the Iraqi Gulf War reparations commission in Geneva.
-- Jean-Pierre Halbwachs of Mauritius, controller, to replace Yukio Takasu of Japan, who resigned.
-- Hedi Annabi of Tunisia, peacekeeping.
-- Alvaro de Soto of Peru, political affairs.
-- Manfred Eisele of Germany, peacekeeping.
-- Denis Halliday of Ireland, human resources.
-- Samir Sanbar of Lebanon, department of public information.
-- Benon Sevan of Cyprus, conference and support services.
